note: 008 Strait of Hormuz (Bidhan's decision 2026-11-23): strictly neutral geography + shipping, 'Press the button' what-if (no conflict, no militaries, no blame). Voices 008 rotation: Roger (M, narrator) + Matilda (F, presses the button).
lines: This is the busiest oil doorway on Earth. And it's only 21 miles wide.
This is the busiest OIL DOORWAY on Earth. And it's only 21 MILES wide.
21 miles? That's a commute, not an ocean.
21 MILES? That's a COMMUTE, not an ocean.
And the lanes are even tighter. Two miles going in, two miles coming out, and a two-mile gap in between.
And the LANES are even tighter. TWO MILES going in, TWO MILES coming out, and a TWO-MILE gap in between.
The biggest tankers are about as long as the Eiffel Tower is tall.
The biggest TANKERS are about as long as the EIFFEL TOWER is tall.
So what does this big red button do?
So what does this BIG RED BUTTON do?
It's a what-if. Press it, and for one day, no ship gets through.
It's a WHAT-IF. Press it, and for ONE DAY, NO SHIP gets through.
Normally, about 20 million barrels of oil pass through here every day.
Normally, about 20 MILLION BARRELS of oil pass through here EVERY DAY.
Around a fifth of all the oil the world uses. And there's no other sea road out of the Gulf.
Around a FIFTH of all the oil the WORLD uses. And there's NO OTHER sea road out of the Gulf.
So just build a pipe around it?
So just build a PIPE around it?
They did. Two pipelines skip the strait. But the spare room in them is only about two and a half million barrels a day.
They DID. Two PIPELINES skip the strait. But the SPARE ROOM in them is only about TWO AND A HALF MILLION barrels a day.
Out of twenty? So the rest just waits?
Out of TWENTY? So the rest just WAITS?
It lines up. Tankers stack up outside, like the world's slowest drive-through.
It LINES UP. Tankers stack up outside, like the world's SLOWEST DRIVE-THROUGH.
Unpressing the button. So a 21-mile gap keeps a fifth of the world's oil moving.
UNPRESSING the button. So a 21-MILE gap keeps a FIFTH of the world's oil moving.
